Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana (BSKY)
Odisha's State Health Assurance Scheme, Explained Simply
A Public Awareness Reference Guide
Important update: Since early 2025, BSKY has been rebranded by the Government of Odisha as the Gopabandhu Jan Arogya Yojana (GJAY), which is now integrated with the central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY scheme. Readers should confirm on the official Odisha Health and Family Welfare portal whether their card or benefits are currently referred to as BSKY or GJAY, as names and processes may have changed since this document was written.
1. Overview
Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana (BSKY) is a state health assurance scheme launched by the Government of Odisha, named after the state's former Chief Minister, Biju Patnaik. It was introduced to reduce the financial burden of hospital treatment on the people of Odisha, especially those from economically weaker sections.
BSKY works in two parts. The first part provides completely free treatment to every resident of Odisha, regardless of income, at all state government health facilities, from the sub-centre level up to district headquarters hospitals and government medical colleges. The second part provides cashless health insurance-style coverage for treatment at empanelled private hospitals, mainly for families holding a ration card under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) or the State Food Security Scheme (SFSS).
2. Eligibility
Every resident of Odisha, regardless of income or social category, is eligible for free treatment at state government hospitals and health centres under the first part of BSKY.
For cashless treatment at empanelled private hospitals under the second part, eligibility is generally linked to holding a valid NFSA or SFSS ration card, which serves as the basis for BSKY coverage rather than a separate BSKY database.
There is no specific age limit for availing BSKY benefits, and coverage applies to the whole family listed on the ration card.
Because BSKY does not require a separate income or category-based application for most families, many households are automatically considered eligible once their ration card details are verified.
3. Benefits
Health coverage of up to five lakh rupees per family per year, with an enhanced limit of up to ten lakh rupees for women beneficiaries, for treatment costs within Odisha.
Cashless treatment at a network of empanelled government and private hospitals, so families do not need to pay upfront and later claim reimbursement.
Coverage for a large number of surgical procedures and medical treatments, including major illnesses, without requiring a specific waiting period, and generally without a cap on room rent.
Coverage for pre-existing health conditions from the time the card becomes active, similar in spirit to central schemes.
Support is available through Swasthya Mitras or similar help-desk staff posted at hospitals to assist beneficiaries with the process.
The exact list of covered procedures, hospital network, and financial limits may be revised periodically by the state government, so beneficiaries should confirm current details for their specific treatment need directly with an empanelled hospital or the official portal.
4. How to Apply
In most cases, there is no separate enrolment process for BSKY. Families already covered under NFSA or SFSS ration cards are automatically considered eligible and are expected to receive a BSKY smart health card.
Check whether your family already has a BSKY smart health card at home; this is usually distributed by the state government along with information campaigns.
If the card has not been received, visit the nearest Mo Seva Kendra (a citizen service centre) with your NFSA or SFSS ration card to request the BSKY card.
For treatment, visit any empanelled government or private hospital, show your BSKY card (or the ration card, where accepted) along with identity proof, and hospital staff or a Swasthya Mitra will assist with verification.
For queries or to check claim status, beneficiaries can contact the official helpline numbers or use the state's official health portal or app.
5. How BSKY Compares with Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY)
For several years after the central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY scheme was launched in 2018, the Odisha government chose to run BSKY as its own separate state scheme rather than adopting PM-JAY, citing BSKY's coverage for all residents at government facilities and its higher coverage limit for women as reasons for the state's approach.
From 2025 onwards, Odisha has joined Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and integrated it with its own state scheme, now referred to as the Gopabandhu Jan Arogya Yojana (GJAY). Under this integrated arrangement, families in Odisha are intended to benefit from both the central government's funding and hospital network under PM-JAY, as well as the state-specific features that BSKY previously offered, such as free care at all government facilities and enhanced coverage for women. Because this transition is relatively recent, some processes, card names, and hospital networks may still be settling into place, so beneficiaries should verify their current entitlement and the correct scheme name with local health authorities.
6. Source Basis
This document is based on general, publicly available information about the Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana as described by the Government of Odisha's Health and Family Welfare Department, along with public reporting on its subsequent integration with Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY. No specific figures, dates, or claims that could not be reasonably confirmed have been included; all content has been rewritten in simple language and should be verified against the official scheme website for the latest details.

National Health Authority (NHA), Government of India — Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY — www.pmjay.gov.in
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India (MoHFW) — www.mohfw.gov.in
National Health Mission (NHM), Odisha — www.nhmodisha.gov.in
This content is for general awareness only. Please verify current details on the official scheme website before applying.
